SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::triangular_solve¶

Back to SeriesLinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::triangular_solve(
    const Series& b, bool upper = true, bool unitriangular = false) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::triangular_solve(
    bool upper = true, bool unitriangular = false) const

What It Does¶

Solves A X = B when the owning Series is triangular. The method uses backward substitution for an upper triangle and forward substitution for a lower triangle, avoiding a general matrix factorization.

Solving One Known Variable At A Time¶

Triangular structure orders the unknowns. In a lower-triangular system the first equation determines the first variable, then each following equation uses values already found. Upper-triangular systems proceed in reverse. This is why triangular solves are the final stage of QR, Cholesky, and LU methods.

Parameters¶

b (const Series&) Vector [...,n] or matrix [...,n,k] of right-hand sides. A vector result is represented as a column with shape [...,n,1].

upper (bool, default true) Read the upper triangle when true; read the lower triangle when false.

unitriangular (bool, default false) Treat every diagonal entry as exactly one. Stored diagonal values are ignored, so no division by them occurs.

Batch dimensions of A and B broadcast; matrix dimensions do not.

Gradient¶

For incoming sensitivity G, dB = A^-T G and dA = -(A^-T G) X^T, restricted to the triangle actually used. Both the factor and right-hand side can track slopes; ignored unit diagonals receive no sensitivity.

Examples¶

Example 1. Solve a lower-triangular system with a vector right-hand side.

auto l = pluss::make_series({{2.0, 0.0}, {1.0, 3.0}});
auto b = pluss::make_series({2.0, 7.0});
std::cout << l.linearalg.triangular_solve(b, false) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[1],
  [2]]

Example 2. Unit-triangular mode ignores deliberately nonsensical diagonal storage.

auto l = pluss::make_series({{99.0, 0.0}, {2.0, -7.0}});
std::cout << l.linearalg.triangular_solve(
    pluss::make_series({3.0, 8.0}), false, true) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[3],
  [2]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The default is upper=true; pass false for a Cholesky lower factor.

  • Entries outside the selected triangle are ignored, not validated as zero.

  • A zero used diagonal makes the system singular unless unit-triangular mode bypasses it.

  • Vector right-hand sides gain a trailing singleton dimension.

See Also¶

  • qr_r: produce an upper-triangular factor.

  • cholesky_solve: perform both triangular stages for an SPD system.
